obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Primary text, heading type, dark icons, and the strongest foreground layer

carbon.$description: Carbon — Filled primary buttons, active nav state, dark surface fill

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary headings, button labels on light surfaces, heavy icon strokes

slate.$description: Slate — Body secondary text, helper copy, muted metadata

ash.$description: Ash — Tertiary text, disabled states, placeholder copy, subtle borders

fog.$description: Fog — Inactive icons, low-emphasis dividers, shadow tinting

pebble.$description: Pebble — Icon strokes on neutral surfaces, muted glyph color

smoke.$description: Smoke — Heavy body text where Obsidian feels too sharp, small caption emphasis

charcoal-veil.$description: Charcoal Veil — Navigation bar text and borders — the dark nav strip registers as a separate layer

dusk.$description: Dusk — Deep surface fill for elevated dark blocks and image overlays

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas — barely-there warm/lavender tint that separates the site from pure white

bone.$description: Bone — Card surfaces, secondary panels, subtle raised containers

mist.$description: Mist — Hairline borders, divider rules, button outlines, input borders

ice-wash.$description: Ice Wash — Pale cool-blue background tint for highlighted cards and feature panels

iris-sweep.$description: Iris Sweep — Brand logo gradient midpoint — the wordmark's signature purple-to-blue sweep

orchid-edge.$description: Orchid Edge — Brand logo gradient start — warm violet anchor of the wordmark sweep

sky-drift.$description: Sky Drift — Brand logo gradient end — cool blue terminus of the wordmark sweep

figtree.$description: Single-family system: 700 carries the hero and section headlines at 48–60px with tight tracking, 600 handles subheadings and prominent labels at 24–34px, 500 covers button labels and emphasized body at 16–18px, 400 runs body and caption copy at 13–16px. The geometric, low-contrast character of Figtree keeps the all-black type from feeling oppressive.
